review_evidence: Codex self-review: pedagogy, answer keys, concept slots, unseen passages, age fit, and source independence
title: Badal and Moti
source_note: NCERT structural alignment only. Zidd uses original teaching passages, checks, and feedback instead of copying the textbook body.

levels.title: Why caring changes the story
levels.teaching_goal: Understand how a kind action at the start of a story can matter later.

guided_check.teaching_block: In this chapter, Badal notices a puppy who needs help. A good answer should name the caring action and explain why it matters.
guided_check.passage: Badal sees a small puppy near the road on a cold evening. He asks his mother if they can care for it.
guided_check.prompt: What kind action does Badal want to take?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: first find who needs help, then find what Badal does for that character.
bridge.passage: The puppy is cold. Badal wants the puppy to be safe at home.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: naming only the kind action leaves a why answer unfinished. Give the action and its reason: Badal cares for the puppy because it is not safe alone.
masterclass.passage: A child finds a young animal in the cold and brings it to a safe place.
masterclass.prompt: Why is bringing the animal to safety a kind action?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now answer without hints. Name the caring action.
independent_check.passage: Badal finds Moti outside and wants to keep him safe.
independent_check.prompt: What does Badal do for Moti?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Carry the need-action-reason pattern into a different kind of care.
transfer_check.passage: Meher sees a new student standing alone with a school map. She walks with him to the library.

concept_slots.description: identifies that the new student needs directions or help
explains that Meher helps him find or reach the library

levels.title: Put story events in order
levels.teaching_goal: Track what happens first, next, and later in a simple story.

guided_check.teaching_block: Story order means following the events step by step. Look for time clues: first Badal meets Moti, later Moti helps people find Badal.
guided_check.passage: First, Badal cares for Moti. Later, Moti barks near the place where Badal needs help.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: first means the earliest event in the story.
bridge.passage: Badal meets Moti before Moti grows and helps him.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: do not choose an event just because you read it first. Follow the dependency: Moti can only help Badal later because Badal cared for him earlier.
masterclass.passage: A child helps a puppy. Later, the puppy alerts adults when the child is in trouble.
masterclass.prompt: Which event must come before the puppy alerts adults?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now order the events without hints.
independent_check.passage: Moti becomes Badal's friend. One day Badal needs help. Moti alerts others.
independent_check.prompt: What happens before Moti alerts others?

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use event order in instructions instead of a friendship story.
transfer_check.passage: Rhea washes a cup, pours in milk, and finally adds sliced banana.
transfer_check.prompt: What does Rhea do after washing the cup but before adding banana?

levels.title: Use -ed action words
levels.teaching_goal: Notice action words that show something already happened.

guided_check.teaching_block: Many story actions already happened. In English, many past actions end with -ed: played, helped, thanked.
guided_check.passage: Badal helped Moti. Moti barked loudly.
guided_check.prompt: Which word shows an action that already happened?

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: look for the action word with -ed.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: add -ed only once. Help becomes helped, not helpeded, when the action already happened.
masterclass.passage: Today I help. Yesterday I helped.
masterclass.prompt: Which word means the action happened yesterday?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now write the past action word without hints.
independent_check.prompt: Fill the blank with the past action word.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use regular past tense in a new topic.
transfer_check.passage: Every day we plant seeds. Last Saturday we ___ marigolds.
transfer_check.prompt: Complete the sentence with the past form of plant.

levels.title: Question or statement
levels.teaching_goal: Separate asking sentences from telling sentences.

guided_check.teaching_block: A question asks something and usually ends with a question mark. A statement tells something and ends with a full stop.
guided_check.passage: Can Moti stay with us? Moti is safe now.

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: the question mark is the clue for an asking sentence.
bridge.prompt: What mark should an asking sentence end with?

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: do not decide from one word alone. A question asks for an answer and ends with a question mark; a statement tells information.
masterclass.prompt: Is this a question or a statement?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now identify the sentence type without hints.

transfer_check.teaching_block: Apply asking-sentence rules in a school situation.
transfer_check.passage: The class pet needs fresh water. You want to ask who will fill its bowl.
transfer_check.prompt: Write the question you would ask the class.

concept_slots.description: uses who or another clear asking form
asks about filling or bringing water for the bowl

levels.title: Tell the main idea
levels.teaching_goal: Say what the chapter is mostly about in your own words.

guided_check.teaching_block: The main idea is not one tiny detail. It is what most of the story is about.
guided_check.passage: Badal cares for Moti. Moti becomes his friend and later helps when Badal is in trouble.
options: kindness and friendship can help us
accepted_answers: kindness and friendship can help us

bridge.teaching_block: Bridge support: choose the idea that covers the beginning and the ending.
bridge.passage: Badal helps Moti first. Moti helps Badal later.

masterclass.teaching_block: Masterclass: one interesting detail is not the main idea. Use your own words for an idea that covers the beginning and ending.
masterclass.passage: Two friends care for each other at different moments.
masterclass.prompt: Which answer is a main idea?

independent_check.teaching_block: Now write the chapter idea in your own words.
independent_check.passage: Badal and Moti both show care when the other one needs help.
independent_check.prompt: What is this chapter mostly about?

concept_slots.description: refers to Badal and Moti or both friends
states that they care for or help one another

transfer_check.teaching_block: Use the main-idea strategy in a different friendship.
transfer_check.passage: Asha explains a maths step to Kunal. The next day, Kunal lends Asha his notes when she misses class.
transfer_check.prompt: Write the main idea of this short passage.

concept_slots.description: states that friends help or support one another
covers learning help and shared notes rather than one detail

items.passage: Moti limps after stepping on a thorn. Badal calls an adult and keeps Moti still.
items.prompt: Why does Badal keep Moti still?
options: to avoid hurting the paw more
accepted_answers: to avoid hurting the paw more
so the paw is not hurt more

items.passage: A puppy cannot reach a bowl on a high step. Nila places the bowl on the floor.
items.prompt: Explain why Nila's action is caring.

concept_slots.description: identifies the puppy's need or the bowl being too high
explains that moving the bowl lets the puppy reach, eat, or drink

items.passage: Badal leaves a shaded bowl of water outside on a hot afternoon.
items.prompt: Which need is Badal meeting?

items.passage: A neighbour notices that Moti's leash is caught around a chair leg and gently frees it.
items.prompt: Tell why the neighbour's action helps Moti.

concept_slots.description: mentions that Moti or the leash is caught or stuck
explains that freeing the leash lets Moti move safely

items.passage: Badal opens the gate, clips on Moti's lead, and then begins the walk.
items.prompt: What happens just before the walk begins?

items.passage: After Moti drinks, he curls up on the mat.
items.prompt: Name the earlier event.

items.passage: Ravi packed a torch before he entered the dark shed. He switched it on inside.
items.prompt: What did Ravi do before entering the shed?

items.passage: The bell rang. The children lined up. Next, their teacher opened the door.
items.prompt: What happened between the bell and the door opening?

items.passage: Yesterday Badal ___ the loose gate.
items.prompt: Choose the past form of fix.

items.passage: Last evening Moti ___ at a strange sound.
items.prompt: Write the past form of bark.

items.passage: Today we wash the bowls. Yesterday we ___ them.
items.prompt: Which word completes the sentence?

items.passage: The puppy rests now. In the morning, it ___ beside the door.
items.prompt: Write the past form of rest.

items.passage: Why is Moti barking___
items.prompt: Choose the correct end mark.

items.passage: Badal checks the latch each night___
items.prompt: Write the end mark for this statement.

items.passage: You want to know where Moti sleeps.
items.prompt: Which sentence asks clearly?

items.passage: You want to know whether Badal filled the water bowl.
items.prompt: Write a complete question to ask Badal.

concept_slots.description: uses a clear yes-no question form
asks about filling the water bowl

items.passage: Rohan cares for an old dog every morning. The dog waits by the gate and warns Rohan when a bicycle comes too close.
items.prompt: Which main idea fits both events?

items.passage: Badal makes space for Moti in his home. Moti later stays beside Badal when he is unwell. Their actions show trust over time.
items.prompt: Summarise the friendship in your own words.

concept_slots.description: mentions Badal and Moti or the friends
states that care, trust, or help goes both ways

items.passage: A child gives a stray kitten food and a dry box. Weeks later, the kitten follows the child home when she takes a wrong turn.
items.prompt: What message joins the beginning and ending?
options: Kindness can grow into loyal help.
accepted_answers: Kindness can grow into loyal help.
kindness can grow into loyal help

items.passage: Nitin helps Eva practise reading. Eva later helps Nitin organise his science chart. Each friend shares a different strength.
items.prompt: Write the main idea without listing every detail.

concept_slots.description: identifies the people as friends or partners
states that they help each other with different strengths
